chunks: You will never attain piety until you spend from what you love; and whatever you spend of anything, indeed Allah is Knowing of it.

key_terms.الْبِرَّ: Piety or goodness, specifically referring to the highest degree of virtue
key_terms.مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ: From what you love (indicating spending cherished possessions)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for attaining true piety (Birr) according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the event of the Prophet giving away his best garment or Ali ibn Abi Talib donating his ring in charity while bowing in prayer, highlighting the pinnacle of selflessness (ikhlas). It distinguishes between mere obligatory almsgiving and voluntary sacrifice from one's most cherished possessions, serving as a criterion for true righteousness. The mention of God's knowledge underscores that the spiritual value of the act lies in the giver's detachment from worldly attachment.
